title: Synthesis and Application of a Clickable Epoxomicin-Based Probe for Proteasome Activity Analysis
protocol: Synthesize the Thr-Ile-Ile peptide fragment using standard solid-phase conditions following Fmoc-based synthesis from C- to N-terminus.
Attach a PEG2 linker to the synthesized Thr-Ile-Ile peptide fragment.
Add an N-methyl propargyl amine via bromoacetic acid coupling.
Cleave the compound from the high loading Wang-Thr resin.
Precipitate the crude material using cold diethyl ether.
Dry the precipitated material.
Weigh Fmoc-Thr(tBu)-Wang resin in fritted syringe.
Cap bottom of syringe and add 2 ml DMF to cover resin beads.
Insert syringe plunger and push gently to maximize contact between resin beads and solvent.
Incubate the syringe for 30 to 60 min at room temperature with shaking.
Remove the plunger and place syringe on manifold to drain the solvent.
Cap bottom of syringe and add 2 ml of 20% piperidine in DMF to deprotect Fmoc group.
Place syringe plunger back into the syringe and incubate for 30 min at room temperature with shaking.
Put syringe on a manifold and drain the solution.
Wash resin three times with 2 to 5 ml of DMF.

Perform a Kaiser test by adding 1 to 2 drops of each of the 3 Kaiser reagents into a small round-bottom rimless glass tube and transferring a small amount of resin beads from the syringe to the glass tube.
Heat the glass tube at ≥95°C for 5 min and check the color of the beads: A dark blue/purple coloration indicates a positive result (presence of primary amines).
Use a white-light microscope to examine the beads more closely if necessary.
Repeat steps 6–8 if the Kaiser test yields partial or no color change in the resin beads.
Weigh out 4 equivalents of Fmoc-Ile-OH and 4 equivalents of HBTU, then dissolve them in 2 ml DMF.
Add 8 equivalents of DIPEA to the mixture; a coloration indicates activation of amino acid.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly and add the solution to the resin.
Incubate the syringe for 1 hr at room temperature.
Repeat steps 5–10 using Fmoc-Ile-OH once again.
Repeat steps 5–10 using PEG2 linker.
Weigh out enough BAA to make 1 ml of a 2 M solution in dry DMF.
Prepare 1 ml of 1 M DIC in dry DMF.
Mix BAA and DIC solutions and agitate until a white precipitate is observed.
Cap the bottom of the syringe.
Add the 2 ml mixture of activated BAA to the syringe.
Insert the plunger.
Incubate at 37°C for 20 min with shaking.
Drain solution from the resin.
Wash resin three times with 2 ml anhydrous DMF.
Perform the Kaiser test; ensure the result is negative.
Prepare 1.5 ml of a 1 M solution of N-methylpropargylamine in anhydrous DMF.
Add prepared solution to the resin and incubate at 37°C for 1 hr with shaking.
Wash resin three times with 2 ml DMF.
Wash resin three times with DCM.
Allow the resin to dry by pulling vacuum through the syringe.
Cleave peptide from resin by adding 3 ml of cleavage solution and incubating the syringe at room temperature for 2 hr.
Collect resulting solution in a conical tube.
Wash beads three times with 3 ml DCM.
Place a stream of argon/nitrogen over the top of the solution to evaporate solvents until a viscous residue remains.
Add prechilled diethyl ether to the crude material and centrifuge at 4500 × g for 10 min.
Decant the diethyl ether.
Vacuum-dry the resulting product until a solid is observed.
Store the product at −20°C.
Protect the Thr hydroxyl group using conventional coupling reagents in tetrahydrofuran (THF).
Dry the crude material under vacuum.
Resuspend the dried material in methanol (MeOH) for reverse-phase HPLC purification.
Lyophilize the final compound overnight.
Resuspend the final compound in dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO).
Place a stir bar inside each glass vial and place them in an oven at 95°C the day before the experiment.
Weigh out compound (2) and dissolve it in 1 ml of anhydrous THF in Vial A.
Flush argon/nitrogen into Vial A and cap it tightly.
Weigh out 2 equivalents of TBSCl and 2.2 equivalents of imidazole, then add them to Vial A.
Flush argon/nitrogen into Vial A again after adding the reagents and cap it.
Place Vial A on a stir plate and allow the mixture to stir for 18 hours.
Weigh 1.05 equivalents of HBTU and 1.05 equivalents of HOBt, then add them to Vial A.
Add 3 equivalents of DIPEA to Vial A after adding HBTU and HOBt.
Flush argon/nitrogen into Vial A once more after adding DIPEA and cap it tightly.
Place vial A on stir plate and allow the mixture to react for 30 min.
Weigh 1.05 equivalents of (S)-2-Amino-4-methyl-1-((r)-2-methyloxiran-2-yl)pentan-1-2,2,2-trifluoroacetate and add them to oven-dried vial B.
Dissolve the mixture in 0.5 ml anhydrous THF then add 3 equivalents of DIPEA.
Flush argon/nitrogen inside vial B and cap.
Place vial on stir plate and allow the mixture to react for 5 to 10 min.
Transfer solution from vial B to vial A and allow the mixture to react at room temperature for 4 to 5 hr.
Rinse vial B with additional 0.5 ml dry THF to ensure complete transfer of material.
Concentrate crude material in rotary evaporator and redissolve in MeOH.
Purify crude solution by reverse-phase HPLC coupled to a UV-Vis detector at 210 nm.
Use mobile phases (A) 95% Water/5% Acetonitrile/0.5% TFA and (B) 95% Acetonitrile/5% Water with 0.5% TFA.
Identify peaks corresponding to the product material by LC/MS.
Combine fractions containing the desired compound.
Concentrate combined fractions in a rotary evaporator to remove ACN and TFA.
Freeze the solution at -80°C.
Lyophilize until a powder is obtained.
Weigh out the required compound and place it in a glass vial.
Dissolve the weighed compound in 0.5 ml of a 1:1 DMSO:H2O mixture.
Cap the vial containing the dissolved compound.
Weigh 1 equivalent of an azide-containing fluorophore, 0.1 equivalents of copper sulfate pentahydrate, and 1 equivalent of sodium ascorbate.
Prepare a concentrated solution of each solid if necessary: prepare 1 µmol solutions in DMSO (fluorophore) at 10 mM, DI water for sodium ascorbate and copper sulfate pentahydrate both at 10 mM.
Add the prepared solutions to a glass vial containing the fragment.
Place a stir bar inside the vial.
Flush the vial with argon/nitrogen.
Degas the mixture by placing it in a sonicator bath for 5 min.
Flush the vial again with argon/nitrogen and cap it.
Place the vial on a hot plate and allow the mixture to react at 80°C for 1 hr while stirring.
Reconstitute the fluorophore of choice if thermolabile, using THPTA at 37°C.
Purify the crude solution by reverse-phase HPLC coupled to a UV-Vis detector at 210 nm.
Identify peaks corresponding to the product material by LC/MS.
Combine fractions containing the desired compound and concentrate them in a rotary evaporator.
Freeze the concentrated solution at −80°C.
Lyophilize the frozen solution until a powder is obtained.
Store the powder as is or dissolved in DMSO at −20°C for future testing.
Culture HEK-293T cells (ATCC® CRL-3216TM) and plate them.
Add activity-based probes to the cells, with or without candidate modulators.
Incubate the samples according to the protocol.
Prepare samples for separation and analysis by SDS-PAGE.
Retrieve a frozen vial of HEK-293T cells from the freezer and thaw in a water bath at 37°C.
Transfer the cell suspension to a sterile 15-ml conical tube and gradually dilute it to 10 ml using DMEM with 10% FBS.
Centrifuge the conical tube at 300 × g for 3 to 5 min to pellet the cells.
Vacuum aspirate the medium from the tube and resuspend the pellet in 10 ml DMEM with 10% FBS.
Transfer the solution to a T-75 culture flask and place it in the CO2 incubator.
Check the culture flask periodically for cell health and density using an upright, bright-light microscope.
Once 80% to 90% confluency is reached, remove the flask from the incubator and vacuum aspirate the medium.
Add 10 ml of 1× PBS to the culture flask to wash the cells and then vacuum aspirate the solution.
Add 1 ml of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA solution and return the flask to the incubator for 3 to 5 min.
Visually inspect the culture flask to ensure complete detachment of the cells.
Dilute the suspension with 9 ml DMEM with 10% FBS.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15-ml conical tube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min to pellet the cells.
Vacuum aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 10 ml DMEM with 10% FBS by pipetting up and down.
Take 30 to 50 µl of the cell suspension and transfer to a 0.6-ml tube.
Place the glass coverslip on top of the hemocytometer and gently fill the chambers underneath.
Place the hemocytometer under the bright-light microscope and count cells to determine the amount of cells per ml.
Prepare stock cell suspension based on the plate and number of samples to be used.
Aliquot the stock cell suspension into the plate wells.
Gently shake the stock cell suspension every 3–5 wells.
Visually inspect the plate under the upright, bright-light microscope to ensure plating of the cells and consistency within wells.
Allow the plate to incubate until 90% to 95% confluency is achieved.
Remove the plate from the incubator and dose each well with the synthesized activity-based probe.
Place the plate back in the CO2 incubator for 1 hr.
Prepare stock solutions of molecules to be tested for proteasome modulation.
Incubate stock solutions for at least 1 hour before adding the activity-based probe.
Replace medium in cells with fresh medium containing small molecules and/or chemical probes.
Remove plate from incubator and vacuum aspirate medium from each well.
Add M-PERTM lysis buffer with 100X HaltTM protease cocktail to each well.
Agitate the plate on an orbital shaker for 10 minutes.
Dissolve 5 mg of poly-D-lysine hydrobromide in 50 ml of autoclaved Milli-Q water (100 μg/ml) if partial cell detachment is observed.
Filter sterilize the resulting solution.
Store excess poly-D-lysine solution at 4°C.
Add solution to each well based on the plate type specified in Table 2.
Let the plate sit for 5 to 30 minutes at room temperature.
Vacuum aspirate the solution from each well.
Rinse the surface twice using the same volume of PBS.
Collect cell lysate in Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 10 minutes and 4°C to pellet cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant to fresh new tubes.
Measure the protein concentration following the method of choice.
Aliquot samples so that the total protein is equal among them.
Prepare loading buffer using 4× Laemmli sample buffer according to manufacturer instructions.
Add the necessary volume to each sample.
Briefly vortex the samples to mix the loading buffer with the lysates.
Heat samples in a 95°C heat block for 5 to 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples briefly.
Load the samples into a 10-well, 50-μl/well gradient gel.
Run the gel at 150 V and constant current for 55 min using 1× SDS Tris-HCl glycine running buffer.
Remove the gel cassette from the electrophoresis cell.
Place the gel in a plastic box.
Rinse the gel three times with DI water.
Image the gel using a biomolecular imager suitable for the selected fluorophore.
Coomassie stain the gel for 30 to 60 min to ensure equal protein loading.
Destain the gel for 4 to 24 hr, or until the background is clear.
Incubate cells according to Basic Protocol 4 steps 1-17.
Remove the plate from the incubator.
Dose wells with the synthesized activity-based probe.
Place the plate back in the CO2 incubator for 1 hour.
Remove the plate from the incubator and place on ice.
Vacuum aspirate the DMEM from each well carefully.
Add 200 µl cold PBS to each well and gently dislodge the cells from the bottom of the plate using a cell scraper.
Collect the cell suspensions in a fresh tube and centrifuge at 4°C for 3 min at 300 × g.
Discard supernatant and resuspend in 200 µl of cold PBS.
Centrifuge again as described previously to remove unreacted probe.
Remove supernatant and resuspend in another 200 µl of cold PBS.
Add 20 μl of viability dye to all samples except the unstained and no viability dye controls.
Incubate samples for 20 min at room temperature.
Mix samples by pipetting up and down before analysis.
Record 50,000 events per sample using flow cytometry.
Perform a forward versus side scatter gating in the first level to differentiate cells from debris.
Perform a second level gating in the channel corresponding to the excitation/emission wavelength of the dye to distinguish dead cells from live cells.
Use TO-PROTM 3 Ready FlowTM as a membrane-impermeable dye that binds to double-stranded DNA of dead cells.
